title: EQWorkspace and BandNode — graph, response curves, draggable nodes
description:
Implement the main EQ graph workspace and per-band draggable nodes per SHREDEQ_SPEC.md §13.3, §13.4, §13.8.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY the files listed in this task's allowed_write_paths.

Before editing, inspect:
- .abracapocus/SHREDEQ_SPEC.md §13.3 main EQ workspace overlays, §13.4 band node visual state, §13.8 interaction design
- Source/UI/ShredEQLookAndFeel.* palette colours from j.1
- Source/DSP/ResponseComputer.* magnitude/phase curve API from phase B (read-only consume)
- Source/UI/PercentileCloud.* / ResonancePersistenceMap.* / NoteRulerData.* snapshot getters from phase I (display hooks only)
- Source/ParameterIDs.h band parameter ID patterns
- Source/PluginProcessor.h accessors for band params / response snapshots if present

Implement Source/UI/BandNode.h/.cpp:
1. Component (or lightweight drawable owned by EQWorkspace) representing one parametric band.
2. Visual state: band number, filter-type glyph, stage badge, current gain, dynamic activity ring, M/S or channel routing glyph, tracking indicator, sidechain indicator, bypass dimming, selection highlight.
3. Dynamic nodes: center handle = static gain, outer range handle = max dynamic movement, live position = actual modulated gain when dynamics data available; provide setter APIs even if processor feed is assembled later.
4. Hit-testing helpers for center vs range handle.

Implement Source/UI/EQWorkspace.h/.cpp:
1. juce::Component hosting log-frequency X axis and gain Y axis (±24 dB default).
2. Paint layered in order (each toggleable via bool flags / methods): grid, pre/post spectra placeholders, percentile cloud fill hook, dynamic-range map hook, resonance candidates, note guides, sidechain collision regions, composite / Stage A / adaptive / Stage B response curves, phase response when enabled, BandNode overlays.
3. Interaction (§13.8): double-click empty graph → create bell band callback; modifier+double-click → filter-type selection callback; horizontal drag → frequency; vertical drag → gain; wheel/gesture → Q; modifier drag → fine adjust; drag range handle → dynamic range; Delete → remove selected band callback; headphone/delta icon hit areas call solo / hear-removed callbacks. Wire changes through APVTS attachments or listener callbacks supplied by the editor — do not own PluginEditor.
4. Accept external curve buffers (ResponseComputer output) and analyzer snapshot views without re-owning FFT engines.
5. Coordinate mapping helpers: frequencyToX/xToFrequency (log), gainToY/yToGain (linear dB).
6. Selection model: selectedBandIndex with change callbacks for InspectorPanel consumers.

Do not modify PluginEditor, CMakeLists.txt, or InspectorPanel/IntelligenceDrawer. verification_commands left empty.
acceptance_criteria: EQWorkspace paints a log-frequency vs ±24 dB gain graph with composite response curve drawing path
EQWorkspace exposes toggleable overlay hooks for spectra/percentile/resonance/note/sidechain/phase layers
BandNode visual state includes band number, filter type, stage, gain, dynamic activity, routing, tracking/sidechain indicators, bypass and selection
Dynamic band handles distinguish static gain center, max dynamic range outer handle, and current gain position APIs
EQWorkspace maps drag/wheel interactions to frequency, gain, and Q with fine-adjust modifier support and selection callbacks
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified

allowed: BandNode as Component children or workspace-owned drawables
callback/listener interfaces for create/remove/param change without owning APVTS
placeholder paths when analyzer snapshots are null
±24 dB default gain axis extensible via setter
